additional_requirements.title: Considerations for Web Applications
additional_requirements.text:
## JavaScript

Follow these guidelines for web applications:

- If possible, download and host all application assets, such as JavaScript libraries, CSS stylesheets, and web fonts on your own servers rather than relying on a CDN or external provider. Hosting your assets locally would mitigate the risk of remote manipulation of the content.
- If fetching scripts from the remote servers is inevitable, use encrypted channels only (HTTPS).
- Perform integrity checks through nonces and hashes. See these [guidelines](/library/tasks/T331/) for using CSP headers for checking hashes and nonces.


## Subresource Integrity (SRI)

If you need features provided by an external provider, you may also use __Subresource Integrity (SRI)__ to mitigate against external manipulation of your assets.

SRI is a security feature that enables browsers to verify that files they fetch (such as from a CDN) are delivered without unexpected manipulation. It works by allowing you to provide a cryptographic hash that a fetched file must match.

Note that not all browsers support SRI. To check the compatibility of different browsers, refer to this [Mozilla article](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Subresource_Integrity).
